transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Lately when I’m home alone, I end up eating way more food at once than I think most people would, and it keeps happening. It's just gotten really hard to handle on my own, so I thought I should probably talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to prevent weight gain by doing things like making yourself throw up, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things to make up for the food. I don't throw up, fast, or try to exercise it off—in fact, I've actually been avoiding playing pickup basketball or doing any sports lately because I feel so bad about myself. I just end up sitting in my room feeling miserable.
How often do these episodes of eating a large amount of food typically happen in a week, and how many months has this been going on?

This has been going on for about five months now, starting after I moved back home from college. For at least the last three or four months, it's been happening at least once a week, and honestly, often more than that.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much faster than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating even when you aren't actually hungry?

Yeah, I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing and just shoveling the food in between gaming rounds until it's all gone in like ten minutes. I also keep eating way past being full, to the point where my stomach actually hurts and I have to lie back on my bed because I'm so stuffed and uncomfortable.
When you have these eating episodes, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed by how much you're consuming? And do you feel disgusted or very guilty afterward?

Yes, I always wait until my parents are asleep or out to eat in my room with the door closed, because I'm so embarrassed by how much I'm putting away. Afterward, I just sit there staring at the pile of wrappers feeling completely gross, guilty, and angry at myself for doing it again.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Binge Eating Disorder (ICD-10: F50.81). He describes recurrent episodes of eating objectively large amounts of food accompanied by a sense of lack of control, occurring at least once a week for the past 3 to 4 months. These episodes are characterized by eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until uncomfortably full, eating alone due to embarrassment, and feeling disgusted, guilty, and angry with himself afterward.
